# Test: Friendship and siblings
id: friendship-siblings
time: 25

## Part 1
figure: study-timeline | Figure 1: when the researchers took their measurements
### Passage: Study links early friendships with sibling relationships
A new {{longitudinal|theo dõi dài hạn|following the same people over a long period of time|ex: The longitudinal survey asked the same students questions every year for ten years.}} study has found that children who form close friendships
outside the home during their primary-school years tend to develop warmer,
less {{conflict-ridden|đầy mâu thuẫn|full of arguments and disagreements|ex: Their conflict-ridden meeting ended without any decision.}} relationships with their siblings by early adolescence.
Researchers followed just over four hundred families for eight years,
recording both peer relationships and sibling dynamics at regular intervals.

The lead researcher, Dr. Elena Kramer, suggests that the skills children
practise with friends — {{negotiation|sự thương lượng|talking with someone to reach an agreement|ex: After a long negotiation, the two boys agreed to share the bike.|key}}, turn-taking, and repairing
disagreements — {{transfer|chuyển sang, áp dụng sang|(of a skill) move from one situation and be used in another|ex: Skills you learn in sport can transfer to your studies.|key}} directly into the sibling relationship, which
often lacks the {{voluntary|tự nguyện|done because you choose to, not because you must|ex: Joining the school club is voluntary.|key}} nature of a chosen friendship. Because siblings
cannot simply {{walk away from|bỏ đi, rời bỏ (một tình huống)|leave a difficult situation instead of dealing with it|ex: You can't just walk away from your problems.|key}} a disagreement the way friends sometimes can,
children who have already rehearsed conflict-resolution strategies
elsewhere appear better {{equipped|có đủ khả năng, được trang bị (kỹ năng)|having the skills or knowledge you need to do something|ex: After the course, she felt well equipped to start her new job.}} to apply them at home.

Interestingly, the study found no equivalent effect running in the other
direction: having a positive sibling relationship in early childhood did
not reliably predict friendship quality later on. The authors caution that
the finding does not establish {{causation|quan hệ nhân quả|the fact that one thing makes another thing happen|ex: Two things happening together does not always show causation.|key}}, and that shared family
{{temperament|tính khí|a person's natural character, for example calm or easily angry|ex: My sister has a calm temperament and rarely gets upset.|key}} could still explain part of the pattern. A {{follow-up study|nghiên cứu tiếp theo|a later study that continues an earlier one|ex: The doctors plan a follow-up study to see if the patients stay healthy.|key}} is
planned to track the same {{cohort|nhóm đối tượng (nghiên cứu)|a group of people who are studied together over time|ex: The researchers met the same cohort of students every year.}} into late adolescence.

### Questions: tfng
instructions: Do the following statements agree with the information given in the passage?

Q. The study followed families for less than five years.
A. FALSE
W. Para 1: "followed just over four hundred families for eight years."

Q. Dr. Kramer believes friendship skills carry over into sibling relationships.
A. TRUE
W. Para 2: skills "transfer directly into the sibling relationship."

Q. The researchers proved that sibling relationships cause friendship quality.
A. NOT GIVEN
W. Para 3: the authors explicitly say the finding does not establish causation, and no claim about sibling→friendship causation is made either way.

limit: NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS
instructions: Complete the sentences below using words from the passage.

Q. Unlike friendships, sibling relationships are not ______.
A. voluntary
W. Para 2: "lacks the voluntary nature of a chosen friendship."

Q. The researchers plan a ______ to follow the same group of children further.
A. follow-up study | follow up study
W. Para 3: "A follow-up study is planned."

### Questions: mcq
instructions: Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D.
figure: finding-chart | Figure 2: which direction the effect ran

Q. According to the passage, why might siblings be more motivated than friends to resolve conflict poorly at first?
A) They are legally required to live together
B) They cannot easily exit the relationship the way friends can
C) They are usually the same age
D) They spend more hours per day together
A. B
W. Para 2: siblings "cannot simply walk away from a disagreement the way friends sometimes can."

### Questions: mcq_multi
count: 2
instructions: Which TWO of the following are mentioned as possible explanations or limitations of the study? Choose TWO letters.
options:
A. The sample size was too small to be meaningful
B. Shared family temperament might explain some results
C. The study does not prove causation
D. The children were not followed for long enough
E. The researchers only studied only children

Q.
A. B | C
W. Para 3 raises both the causation caveat and the temperament explanation.

## Part 2
### Passage: Emma and Jack's social media habits
Emma checks her social media accounts several times a day. She posts
photographs most evenings, comments on friends' updates, and does most of
her clothes shopping through links she finds while {{scrolling|lướt (màn hình)|moving up or down a screen to see more content|ex: He spent an hour scrolling through photos on his phone.}}.

Jack, her older brother, {{takes a different approach|có cách làm khác|deals with something in another way|ex: Our new teacher takes a different approach and uses games in every lesson.}}. He opens the same
apps only about once a week, mainly to read what other people have
posted. He has never made {{a post of his own|một bài đăng của riêng mình|a message or photo that he himself puts online|ex: Mia shared a post of her own about her holiday.|key}}, and says he prefers talking
to people {{in person|trực tiếp, gặp mặt|by being physically there, face to face|ex: I'd rather meet the new teacher in person than send an email.|key}} rather than online.

![Figure 3: how often each of them opens an app](#habits-chart)

## Part 3
### Passage: How water climbs a plant
Water enters a plant through its roots and travels upward through narrow tubes
called {{xylem|mạch gỗ|the tubes that carry water up through a plant|ex: Water rises through the xylem to every leaf.|key}}. No pump drives it. As water
{{evaporates|bốc hơi|changes from liquid into gas|ex: The puddle evaporated in the sun.}} from tiny pores in the leaves, it pulls the
column of water above it, and the whole chain rises together.

Growers {{take|tính đến|consider something when you make a decision|ex: Please take the weather into account.}} soil temperature {{+into account}} when they
predict how fast a crop will drink, because cold roots take up water slowly.

### Questions: ynng
instructions: Do the following statements agree with the views of the writer?

Q. A plant needs a pump of some kind to raise water.
A. NO
W. Para 1: "No pump drives it."

Q. Cold soil slows how quickly a plant takes up water.
A. YES
W. Para 2: "cold roots take up water slowly."
